title: World Brief · Tuesday, November 10, 2026
subtitle: Prepared 19:02 ET

items.title: Odds of a Fed hike are firming
items.text: After hotter-than-expected core inflation (October CPI +0.4% month over month vs 0.3% expected; core +0.3% vs 0.2%), Governor Waller said he leans toward at least a 25 basis point hike in December and that 50 should be considered; Dallas Fed's Logan argued two more hikes are needed. The Fed meets December 8-9, and short-term yields (2-year +17 bp) are pricing it in.

items.title: Trump: Iran war is "effectively over"; Tehran denies talks
items.text: Trump said new strikes are unlikely but the naval blockade will continue; Iran said no meeting is planned in Qatar. Brent fell below $92, which matters for energy prices and the inflation outlook.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine at the table in Abu Dhabi
items.text: In the first US-mediated meeting since February, Kushner said the sides narrowed the gap between them; the White House is "cautiously optimistic". A headline to watch for European risk and energy.

items.title: Nvidia board investigation
items.text: The board opened an independent investigation into allegations that CEO Jensen Huang was a target of foreign intelligence; Huang acknowledged a mistake in his private life in an email to employees. The stock fell 5.5% and its market value dipped below $4 trillion intraday.

items.title: US politics: post-election tension
items.text: After the midterms in which Democrats won Congress, Trump posted messages questioning the integrity of the results; Republican Rep. Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth.
